ed.c.desc.connections: Each row is one connection: its number on the schema, its type and its two ends (a device with an interface or a port).
ed.c.desc.devices: The nodes of the schema: a node runs an image, the network ones (hub, switch, gateways) have none. For each: how many connections and tasks it has, and what access the participant gets: a web link to its service or a terminal in the browser.
ed.c.desc.variables: The variables of the schema: a constant is the same for all participants, a random one is generated by a pattern for every instance of the lab. The last column lists the devices that use the variable.
ed.c.desc.interfaces: The device's network interfaces: the address mode, the gateway, the number of static routes and the connections. Open an interface to change it.
ed.c.desc.env: The environment variables of the device's service; the participant inside the device always sees them.
ed.c.desc.files: Files are written to the device before the service starts: up to {file} per file and {device} per device with the script.
ed.c.desc.script: Setup commands run as root on a clean device before the service starts, without downloads or package installs.
ed.c.desc.command: The command that starts the service; by default it comes from the image.
ed.c.desc.consolePorts: The management lines of the device; by default {command} as {user} runs on a line. A cable from a serial port of another device plugs in here.
ed.c.desc.serialPorts: Terminal lines inside the device (/dev/ttyCON0): the participant opens them in the terminal, a cable leads to a console port of another device.
ed.c.desc.credentials: Operator logins for the defender's dossier; only the defender sees them.
ed.c.port.removeCredentials: The credentials that name this port ({n}) stay: fix them before publishing.
ed.c.h.credStoredText: the field shows «Value stored»; «Replace» opens a field for a new value. Leave it empty to keep the stored one.

ed.c.port.kernelLogUnavailable: The kernel log can be switched on and published, but a test lab with it cannot be deployed now: no connected laboratory supports it yet.
ed.c.port.val.kernelLogNoPort: The kernel log needs a console port with a program
ed.c.h.kernelLog1: The guest kernel's messages of the microVM on the console line, like on the console of a real device: everything since boot when a client attaches, then new ones.
ed.c.h.kernelLog2: The microvm profile only; shown on the first console port with a program, beside it (the login by default).
